foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption will persist over the next 30 days, with 51% pressure and 74% state confirmation feeding through energy supply shock, supported by 6 urgent critical signals and 4...
foil.perspective_strategic: The 51% pressure and 74% state confirmation indicate a moderately strong transmission path from Red Sea disruption to energy repricing, but the single edge through energy supply shock suggests a contained risk.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 75% confidence level and the absence of directly matched reporting on Red Sea suggest that the energy repricing risk may be overstated, allowing large importers to maintain current pricing without disruption.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 61%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 51% pressure and 74% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
